ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.55 (RydeTAXI mileage for the 4.89 km unexempted detour + the S$0.66 wait over-charge) as a Ryde voucher; note the driver's RD-1 shortest-route breach and remind the driver that a rider's unnamed "stop at a 7-Eleven on the way" does not authorise choosing a far-off-store route.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat (F9–F11), driver statement (F12) and complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation → no safety escalation. Dispute type is fare/route, not safety.

Route: F4 gives one off-route segment, 17:37–17:53, 7.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, +4.89 km, up to 1268 m off route. The only pre-segment rider message (F9, 17:33, before 17:37) is "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes" — the rider did not name a place, and the driver then chose a store that produced the off-route segment (F2 stop at 1.3127/103.8848 is 4.9 km from pickup and 5.2 km from drop-off; the driver says in F12 "I went to the one I know"). Under RD-3(b) the rider's consent is to a stop, not to that route change, so the segment's extra_km is not exempt: ground = scope_other, finding = counts.

No other exemption: F15 records no traffic incidents at all, so RD-4(a) fails; F13/F14 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is not band 1–2 congestion and in any case (RD-4(b)/G3) cannot exempt on its own; F16 fine weather.

RD-2 quantification (RydeTAXI, metered): per-km rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $29.53 ÷ 20.94 = $1.4102/km [F5, F8]. Refund = 4.89 km × $1.4102 = $6.896 ≈ $6.90. The residual gap between the billed 5.47 km excess [F5] and this segment (5.47 − 4.89 = 0.58 km) is not attributable to an identified segment and is not refunded (RD-2).

Waiting fee: the trip is RydeTAXI, so in-trip stop waiting is chargeable at the meter rate, but only for the time actually waited. F2 shows a stationary stop of 4 min 10 s = 4.17 min, while F6 bills 4.6 min. Over-charge = 0.43 min × $0.26/min = $0.11; plus the S$1.19 charge itself is metered waiting under RD-3(c) and stays otherwise. I allow $0.11, i.e. cap the waiting recoverable at S$1.08. (If measured from the chat stop request, the same D7 bound caps the waiting at S$1.08.) Total refund = $6.90 + $0.11 = $7.01.

Driver flag: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; F18 shows the driver's one upheld dispute was a no-show, route upheld = 0, so RD-6 is not met → no flag_account. The driver's breach of the RD-1 shortest-route duty is nonetheless recorded.

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the only pre-segment rider message (F9, 17:33) was sent before the segment began (17:37) and agreed only to a 2-minute stop; the rider named no place, and RD-3(b) says an unnamed stop does not exempt the driver's choice of a far-off store (F12: driver 'went to the one I know'), which produced the off-route segment (F2, F4). Consent scope is 'a stop', not this route change → the segment's extra_km counts under RD-2 (4.89 km × $1.4102 = $6.90). No RD-4 traffic excuse: F15 shows no incidents, F13/F14 only band 4, which cannot exempt alone (RD-4(b)).

RD-3(c) stop duration: RydeTAXI waiting is chargeable at the meter rate, but only for the time actually waited. F2 measures 4 min 10 s stationary while F6 bills 4.6 min; the 0.43-min difference ($0.11) is not covered by any published charge and is refunded.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement that 'the rider asked for a 7-Eleven stop' is accepted only as to the fact a stop was requested; the rider's message (F9) named no place, so under RD-3(b)/RD-5 the driver's own choice of a far-off store is not covered by the rider's consent, and a verbal/after-the-fact justification is not consent.
PIE band 4 (30–39 km/h) is not a band 1–2 LTA congestion record and, per RD-4(b)/G3, cannot exempt a detour on its own; F15 records no traffic incident on the optimal route.
CTE band 4 (30–39 km/h) likewise falls outside the RD-4(a)/(b) conditions and is not tied to the substituted optimal-route portion.
